mainTopic: The intent needed for שופר, who can blow for others, and saying ברכות on behalf of others.
overview: This עמוד finishes the story of רבי זירא asking his attendant to have him in mind while blowing. The גמרא learns from it that the one blowing must have the listener in mind. It defends this view against our משנה about a passerby: there the blower is a שליח ציבור, who has everyone in mind. It also answers a ברייתא that seems to disagree: תנאים argue about this, and רבי זירא follows רבי יוסי. A new משנה then teaches that משה's raised hands and the copper snake had no power of their own. What helped was Israel turning their hearts to their Father in Heaven. The משנה rules that a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן cannot blow for others, because only someone obligated can fulfill a מצוה for others. The גמרא lists who is obligated and explains why כהנים had to be mentioned. It then rules, like רב נחמן, that a half slave, half free person cannot fulfill the מצוה even for himself. Finally, אהבה בריה דרבי זירא teaches when a person may say ברכות for others, and רבא begins a question that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבי זירא tells his attendant to have him in mind
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells his attendant to have intent for him and blow. The גמרא concludes that he holds the משמיע needs כוונה to fulfill the listener's obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Have intent and blow for me.' So it seems רבי זירא holds that the one who blows needs intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי זירא's words to his attendant. From those words it figures out his opinion: the blower must have the listener in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא did not just say 'blow for me.' He said 'have intent and blow.' That extra request shows he thinks the blower's כוונה matters, and not only the listener's. This opinion is what the rest of the section will test.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who makes others hear: the person blowing the שופר
Intent, having something in mind
Apparently / this shows that
He holds (this is his opinion)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the section: does the blower need to have the listener in mind?

phrases.english: Have intent, and blow for me.
phrases.notes: These are רבי זירא's words to his attendant. The story starts on the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: Apparently, he holds:
the one who sounds the shofar needs intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the story of רבי זירא that began on the previous עמוד and draws his opinion from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי זירא, the משמיע must have כוונה to fulfill the listener's obligation.

steps.title: Challenge from the passerby who hears the shofar
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a passerby who hears the שופר is יצא if he had intent. But the blower never had this passerby in mind, so how can that work according to רבי זירא?
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: Someone was passing behind a shul, or his house was next to the shul, and he heard the שופר or the מגילה. If he had intent, he fulfilled his obligation, and if not, he did not. But even if he had intent, so what? The blower did not have him in mind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our משנה to attack רבי זירא. The משנה only checks the listener's intent, even though the blower did not know this passerby was there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes the passerby's כוונה the only thing that decides the case. The blower inside the shul had no idea this man existed. If the blower's intent were required, as רבי זירא says, the passerby should never be יצא.

keyTerms.meaning: They objected (a challenge from a תנאי source)
He fulfilled his obligation
He focused his heart, meaning he had intent
That one / the other person

phrases.english: They objected:
If he was passing behind a synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בֵּיתוֹ סָמוּךְ לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת,
phrases.english: or his house was next to the synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁמַע קוֹל שׁוֹפָר אוֹ קוֹל מְגִילָּה,
phrases.english: and he heard the sound of a shofar or the sound of the Megillah,
if he focused his heart, he fulfilled his obligation,
and if not, he did not fulfill it.
But even if he focused his heart, what of it?

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ לָא קָא מִיכַּוֵּין אַדַּעְתָּא דִּידֵיהּ!
phrases.english: The other one did not have him in mind!
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is the person blowing the shofar inside the shul.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the opinion of רבי זירא that was derived in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's view that the משמיע needs כוונה for the listener.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets a passerby be יצא based only on his own intent, even though the blower could not have had him in mind.

steps.title: The blower is a שליח ציבור who has everyone in mind
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a שליח ציבור, whose intent covers everyone who hears, including the passerby.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a שליח ציבור, who has everyone in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא. The blower in the משנה is the community's שליח ציבור, and he intends to fulfill the obligation of anyone who hears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's rule stays the same: the blower needs intent. A שליח ציבור already has that intent for everyone, even people he does not know about. So the passerby is covered, and the משנה only needs to check the passerby's own intent.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (in this case)
We are dealing with
The community's representative who leads the prayers or blows for everyone

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the blower's intent is unnecessary. A שליח ציבור has intent too. His intent simply covers everyone at once.

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with the community's representative,
whose mind is on everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בִּשְׁלִיחַ צִיבּוּר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by narrowing which case the משנה is talking about.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the blower in the משנה had no one in particular in mind.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blower is a שליח ציבור whose intent covers everyone, so רבי זירא's rule still holds.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא: the blower only needs intent for himself
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא requires both the שומע and the משמיע to have intent. Because it describes the משמיע the same way as the שומע, it seems the blower only needs intent for himself, not for the listener.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If the hearer had intent but the blower did not, or the blower had intent but the hearer did not, he is not יצא until both have intent. The ברייתא describes the blower the same way as the hearer. Just as the hearer has intent for himself, so too the blower has intent for himself. And it says that without this he is not יצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רבי זירא from a ברייתא. It reads the ברייתא to mean the blower only needs to intend his own מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts the שומע and the משמיע side by side. The שומע clearly intends for himself, so the משמיע's intent must also be for himself. That means intent for himself is enough, with no need to have the listener in mind, which contradicts רבי זירא. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof or challenge from a source)
The hearer, the one listening to the שופר
Similar to, parallel with
For himself

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If the hearer had intent but the sounder did not have intent,
or if the sounder had intent but the hearer did not have intent,
he has not fulfilled his obligation,
until both the hearer and the sounder have intent.
It teaches the sounder in the same way as the hearer.
Just as the hearer hears for himself,
so too the sounder sounds for himself,
and it teaches that without this he has not fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: So intent for himself is all the blower needs. He does not have to have the listener in mind, which goes against רבי זירא.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, this brings a fresh challenge against רבי זירא from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's view that the משמיע must have the listener in mind.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the ברייתא puts the שומע and the משמיע side by side, the blower's required intent is only for himself, so intent for the listener is not needed.

steps.title: It is a dispute among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the question is a dispute among תנאים. The תנא קמא says the blower simply blows in his usual way. רבי יוסי says that this applies only to a שליח ציבור, but an individual blower must have intent, just as רבי זירא held.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: the hearer hears for himself, and the blower blows in his usual way. רבי יוסי said: when is this said? For a שליח ציבור. But for an individual, the listener is not יוצא until both the hearer and the blower have intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא by showing that תנאים argue about this question, and רבי זירא follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the blower does not need to think about the listener at all. רבי יוסי makes a distinction: a שליח ציבור's intent already covers everyone, but a private individual must have the listener in mind. Since רבי יוסי contrasts the individual with the שליח ציבור, the 'intent' he requires from the blower must be intent for the listener, which is exactly רבי זירא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים (the sages of the משנה era)
In his usual way, without special intent for the listener
In what case are these words said? This phrase introduces a limitation
A private individual, not leading the community

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says the blower needs no intent for the listener. רבי יוסי says an individual blower does need it, and רבי זירא follows רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim,
as it is taught in a baraita:
The hearer hears for himself,
and the one sounding sounds in his usual way.
Rabbi Yosei said:
In what case are these words said?
For a communal representative,
but with an individual, he has not fulfilled his obligation,
until both the hearer and the sounder have intent.
phrases.notes: This is the same wording as the ברייתא in step 4, but here it is clearly רבי יוסי's view, and רבי זירא follows him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by showing that רבי זירא follows one side of a dispute among תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among תנאים: the challenging view is one opinion, and רבי זירא follows the other (רבי יוסי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say, with no disagreement, that the blower needs intent only for himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: תנאים argue. רבי יוסי requires an individual blower to have intent for the listener, and רבי זירא follows him.

steps.title: משה's raised hands and Israel's hearts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה quotes the פסוק about משה raising his hands in the war against עמלק. It explains that his hands did not win the war. Israel won when they looked upward and directed their hearts to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And when משה raised his hand, Israel prevailed." Did משה's hands make war or break war? Rather, as long as Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they prevailed. If not, they fell.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a lesson from the תורה about the war with עמלק. It asks what משה's raised hands really did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asks a sharp question: hands cannot win or lose a battle on their own. Its answer is that the raised hands led Israel to look up and turn their hearts to ה׳, and that inner focus is what brought victory.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה
But is it so? This opens a question meaning 'surely not'
Looking upward, toward Heaven
Subjecting (fully devoting) their hearts

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying משה's hands were meaningless. It is saying the hands had no power of their own. The real cause of victory was Israel turning their hearts to ה׳.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
"And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand,
that Israel prevailed, etc."
But do the hands of Moses
make war or break war?
Rather, it comes to tell you:
as long as Israel
would look upward
and subject their hearts
to their Father in Heaven,
they would prevail,
and if not, they would fall.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי יָדָיו שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה עוֹשׂוֹת מִלְחָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, which follows the discussion of the intent needed for שופר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel's victory came from turning their hearts to their Father in Heaven, not from משה's hands themselves.

steps.title: The copper snake and healing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a second, similar example. The snake on the pole did not heal anyone by itself. Those who were bitten were healed when they looked upward and directed their hearts to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly: "Make a fiery serpent and put it on a pole, and anyone bitten who sees it will live." Does a snake kill or give life? Rather, when Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they were healed. If not, they rotted away.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second Torah example that teaches the same lesson as משה's hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question and the answer have the same shape as in step 6. An object (a snake on a pole) cannot heal on its own. The healing came through Israel turning their hearts toward ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Similarly. This introduces a parallel case
A fiery serpent
A pole or banner
Rotting or wasting away

steps.whatToRemember: Both examples teach the same point. Physical objects have no power of their own; the real cause is the heart directed to ה׳.

phrases.english: Similarly, you can say:
"Make for yourself a fiery serpent
and set it upon a pole;
and it shall be that everyone who is bitten,
when he sees it, shall live."

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי נָחָשׁ מֵמִית, אוֹ נָחָשׁ מְחַיֶּה?
phrases.english: But does a snake kill, or does a snake give life?
Rather: when Israel
looked upward
and subjected their hearts
to their Father in Heaven,
they were healed,
and if not, they rotted away.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בַּדָּבָר אַתָּה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel example that teaches the same lesson as step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The healing came from Israel turning their hearts to Heaven, not from the snake itself.

steps.title: Who cannot blow for others
steps.stepSummary: The משנה returns to the laws of שופר. A חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן cannot fulfill the obligation for others. The general rule is that anyone not obligated in a מצוה cannot fulfill it for others.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן cannot fulfill the obligation for the many. This is the rule: whoever is not obligated in the matter cannot fulfill the obligation for the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes back to its practical laws and states who cannot blow שופר on behalf of others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three people listed are not obligated in מצוות. The משנה then turns this into a broad principle: to fulfill a מצוה for someone else, you must be obligated in that מצוה yourself.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor
Fulfills the obligation for others
This is the general rule
Obligated in the matter (the מצוה)

steps.whatToRemember: Only someone who is obligated in a מצוה can fulfill it on behalf of others.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle applies far beyond שופר. It is a basic rule for any case where one person fulfills a מצוה for another.

phrases.english: A deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן.
phrases.english: cannot fulfill the obligation on behalf of the many.
This is the principle:
whoever is not obligated in the matter

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן.
phrases.english: cannot fulfill the obligation on behalf of the many.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the Torah lessons of steps 6 and 7 and returns to the practical laws of שופר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone not obligated in a מצוה, such as a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן, cannot fulfill it on behalf of others.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists everyone who is obligated in שופר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. It says that everyone is obligated in שופר, including כהנים, converts, freed slaves, a טומטום, an אנדרוגינוס, and someone who is half slave and half free.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The חכמים taught: Everyone is obligated in blowing the שופר. This includes כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים; גרים and freed slaves; a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס; and someone who is half slave and half free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה by quoting a ברייתא that lists who must hear the שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just taught that anyone not obligated cannot blow for others. So the גמרא first needs to know exactly who is obligated. The list also includes people whose status is unclear, which sets up the next part of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught. This phrase opens a ברייתא.
Obligated
A person whose body is covered, so we cannot tell if he is male or female
A person who has both male and female features
A person who is half slave and half free, for example because one of two owners freed him

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
Everyone is obligated in blowing the shofar.
Kohanim, Levites, and Israelites;
converts and freed slaves;
a tumtum and an androginos;
phrases.notes: Both are people we can't clearly call male or female, and that matters because women are not obligated in שופר.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין.
phrases.english: one who is half slave and half free.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בִּתְקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה from step 8 by listing who is obligated
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone is obligated in שופר, including כהנים, converts, freed slaves, a טומטום, an אנדרוגינוס, and someone who is half slave and half free.

steps.title: Which people of unclear status can blow for others
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A טומטום cannot blow for anyone else. An אנדרוגינוס can blow for another אנדרוגינוס but not for anyone else. A person who is half slave and half free cannot blow for anyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טומטום cannot fulfill the obligation for his own kind or for someone not of his kind. An אנדרוגינוס can fulfill it for his own kind, but not for someone not of his kind. One who is half slave and half free cannot fulfill it for his own kind or for someone not of his kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the משנה's rule: a person who may not be fully obligated cannot blow for someone who is fully obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טומטום might be a woman while the listener is a man, even if the listener is another טומטום, so he cannot blow for anyone. Two אנדרוגינוס people have exactly the same status, so one can blow for the other. With a half slave, the slave half of the blower cannot blow for the free half of the listener.

keyTerms.meaning: Fulfills the מצוה on behalf of someone else
His own kind, meaning someone with the same status
Someone not of his kind, such as a regular man

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of doubt. A טומטום is an unknown: each one might be male or might be female, so two of them can differ. An אנדרוגינוס is always the same mix, so two of them are alike.

phrases.aramaic: טוּמְטוּם — אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא לֹא אֶת מִינוֹ,
phrases.english: A tumtum cannot fulfill the obligation for his own kind,
phrases.notes: Under one טומטום's covering there may be a woman, and under the other's a man.

phrases.english: nor for one who is not of his kind.
An androginos can fulfill it for his own kind,
but not for one who is not of his kind.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין —
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free
cannot fulfill it for his own kind,
nor for one who is not of his kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְטוּם — אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא לֹא אֶת מִינוֹ, וְלֹא אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, explaining what the doubtful cases from the list mean for blowing on behalf of others
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טומטום and a half slave cannot blow for anyone. An אנדרוגינוס can blow only for another אנדרוגינוס.

steps.title: Why say that כהנים, לויים and ישראלים are obligated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the first line of the ברייתא and asks why it needed to say that כהנים, לויים and ישראלים are obligated. If they aren't obligated, who would be?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Everyone is obligated in blowing the שופר: כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים. But that is obvious! If these are not obligated, who is obligated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for saying something that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים, לויים and ישראלים make up the whole regular Jewish people. A ברייתא does not usually waste words, so listing them seems pointless. The next step will explain why it was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said. This is used to quote a line from the ברייתא again so it can be discussed.
It is obvious, so why say it?
Who is obligated?

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This just means the ברייתא we quoted above.

phrases.english: Everyone is obligated in blowing the shofar,
Kohanim, Levites, and Israelites.
It is obvious!
If these are not obligated,
who is obligated?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בִּתְקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר, כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים. פְּשִׁיטָא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening line of the ברייתא from step 9 to question its wording
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that כהנים, לויים and ישראלים are obligated
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These groups are the basic Jewish people. Their obligation is obvious, so stating it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The ברייתא needed to teach that כהנים are obligated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא needed to mention כהנים. Since they blow trumpets in the בית המקדש all year, one might think the one-day מצוה of שופר is only for people who don't blow all year. The ברייתא teaches that כהנים are obligated too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for כהנים. You might have thought: since it is written, 'It shall be a day of blowing for you,' only someone who blows on just one day is obligated. But כהנים blow all year, as it is written, 'And you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings.' So I might say they are not obligated. The ברייתא teaches us that they are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא's list is not pointless, because it teaches something about כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls ראש השנה a 'day of blowing,' as if blowing were special to that one day. כהנים blow trumpets over the קרבנות all year, so one might think the 'day of blowing' does not apply to them. The ברייתא rules out this idea: כהנים are fully obligated in שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed. This explains why something that seems obvious had to be said.
It would enter your mind to say. This introduces a mistaken first thought.
Trumpets, blown by the כהנים over the קרבנות
It teaches us, meaning that the mistaken thought is wrong

phrases.english: It was needed for Kohanim,
since it would enter your mind to say:
since it is written
"It shall be a day of blowing for you,"
one who is involved only
in blowing on one day
is the one who is obligated,
but these Kohanim,
since they are involved in blowing all year,
as it is written:
"And you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings,"
I might say they are not obligated.
So the ברייתא teaches us that they are.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֲנִים אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it is obvious' challenge of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows that the obvious-seeming statement was needed to rule out a reasonable mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק calls ראש השנה a 'day of blowing,' כהנים, who blow trumpets all year, might be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: כהנים are fully obligated in the שופר of ראש השנה.

steps.title: Trumpets are not a shofar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer from step 12: blowing trumpets all year has nothing to do with blowing a שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable? There, it is trumpets, and here, it is a שופר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer from step 12. The כהנים in the בית המקדש blow trumpets, not a שופר, so there was no reason to think they would be exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said: since כהנים blow all year, maybe they don't need the one-day מצוה of שופר. The גמרא answers that this doesn't work, because trumpets and a שופר are different instruments. So the question from step 11 comes back: why did the ברייתא need to mention כהנים?

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? Used to challenge a comparison.
Trumpets, which the כהנים blew in the בית המקדש
There / here

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
There, it is trumpets,
phrases.notes: "There" means the כהנים blowing in the בית המקדש all year, from step 12.

phrases.english: and here, it is a shofar!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם חֲצוֹצְרוֹת וְהָכָא שׁוֹפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 12, that כהנים might be exempt because they blow all year
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The all-year blowing is with trumpets, a different instrument, so it gives no reason to exempt them from שופר.

steps.title: A new reason: כהנים and the יובל link
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא had to mention כהנים because שופר on ראש השנה is linked to שופר of יובל, and כהנים are not fully part of the יובל laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was necessary. You might have thought: since we learned that יובל is the same as ראש השנה for blowing and blessings, whoever is included in the מצוה of יובל is included in the מצוה of ראש השנה. These כהנים are not included in the מצוה of יובל, as we learned: כהנים and לויים may sell forever and redeem forever. So I would say they are not obligated in ראש השנה either. The ברייתא teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to why the ברייתא had to say כהנים are obligated. It builds a 'you might have thought' chain linking ראש השנה to יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה says the שופר and blessings of יובל are the same as ראש השנה. From that link, one might think only people bound by יובל are bound by ראש השנה. Since another משנה shows that כהנים and לויים don't follow the usual יובל land rules, one might exempt them, so the ברייתא tells us they are obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jubilee year, every 50th year, when a שופר is blown
It would enter your mind to say. This opens a mistaken first thought.
We learned in a משנה
They may sell forever and redeem forever
It teaches us otherwise

steps.whatToRemember: כהנים are fully obligated in שופר on ראש השנה, even though they are not fully part of the יובל laws.

phrases.english: Rather, it was necessary:
It would enter your mind to say,
since we learned in a Mishnah:
The Jubilee is the same as Rosh HaShanah
phrases.notes: This is talking about the יום כיפור of the יובל year, when the שופר is blown.

phrases.english: for the blowing and for the blessings,
whoever is included in the מצוה of the Jubilee
is included in the מצוה of Rosh HaShanah,
and these Kohanim,
since they are not included in the מצוה of the Jubilee,
as we learned in a Mishnah:
Kohanim and Levi'im may sell forever
phrases.notes: He means their land sales don't follow the usual יובל rules.

phrases.english: and redeem forever,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: בְּמִצְוָה דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לֹא לִיחַיְּיבוּ
phrases.english: I would say: they should not be obligated in the מצוה of Rosh HaShanah
so it teaches us that they are.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִצְטְרִיךְ: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after step 13 rejected the first one
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason for why the wording was needed (a mistaken first thought the ברייתא comes to rule out)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ראש השנה is linked to יובל, and כהנים are not fully under the יובל laws, they would be exempt from שופר on ראש השנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: כהנים are obligated in שופר on ראש השנה.

steps.title: רב הונא: he can fulfill it for himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line about the half slave, half free person, and רב הונא adds that he can fulfill the מצוה for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who is half slave and half free cannot fulfill the obligation for one of his kind, nor for one not of his kind. רב הונא said: but he does fulfill it for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to another line of the ברייתא from step 10, about the half slave, half free person. רב הונא adds a ruling: even though he can't blow for others, his own blowing counts for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said he can't blow for others, whether they are like him or not. רב הונא reads this to mean that his limit is only about other people, so for himself his blowing works.

keyTerms.meaning: Half slave and half free, for example a slave owned by two partners where only one partner freed him
Fulfills the obligation for someone
His kind, meaning another person in the same half-and-half state
For himself

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free
cannot fulfill the obligation for one of his kind
nor for one not of his kind.
Rav Huna said:
But he does fulfill the obligation for himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא לֹא אֶת מִינוֹ וְלֹא אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כהנים line to the half slave, half free line of the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A half slave, half free person cannot blow for others, but according to רב הונא he fulfills the מצוה for himself.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the same problem applies to himself
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן argues that the reason he can't blow for others also stops him from blowing for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב הונא: Why can't he do it for others? Because the slave side can't fulfill it for the free side. Then for himself too, his own slave side can't fulfill it for his own free side.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רב הונא. He uses the very reason behind the ברייתא to show it applies to the person himself too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He can't blow for others because his slave side is not obligated, and someone not obligated can't fulfill it for someone who is. Inside his own body there is the same mix: a slave side blowing for a free side. So there is no real difference between others and himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The slave side of the person
The free side of the person
What is the difference? Used to challenge a distinction.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rav Huna:
Why is it that he can't do it for others?
Because the slave side cannot come
and fulfill the obligation for the free side;
for himself too,
his own slave side cannot come
and fulfill the obligation for his own free side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא: מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the half slave, half free person fulfills the מצוה for himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason he can't blow for others (a slave side blowing for a free side) applies equally inside himself.

steps.title: רב נחמן: not even for himself
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the half slave, half free person cannot fulfill the מצוה even for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said: even for himself he cannot fulfill the obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: After his challenge, רב נחמן states his own ruling. The half slave, half free person's blowing does not count even for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows straight from the challenge in step 16. Since his slave side can't fulfill it for his free side, his blowing is not good enough for anyone, including himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Even

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said:
Even for himself he cannot fulfill the obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אַף לְעַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב נחמן's ruling, replacing רב הונא's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A half slave, half free person does not fulfill the מצוה of שופר even for himself.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says outright that the half slave, half free person cannot fulfill the מצוה even for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: one who is half slave and half free cannot fulfill the obligation even for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב נחמן said. This backs up his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's view was based on logic. Now a ברייתא states the same ruling openly, so his view stands over רב הונא's.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא. Brings support for a view.

steps.whatToRemember: A person who is half slave and half free cannot fulfill the מצוה of שופר for anyone, not even himself, like רב נחמן and the ברייתא.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free
cannot fulfill the obligation even for himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's ruling in step 17
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that he cannot fulfill the מצוה even for himself
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states the same ruling directly

steps.title: Most blessings can be said for others even after you said them yourself, but not bread and wine
steps.stepSummary: אהבה בריה דרבי זירא teaches a ברייתא: for all ברכות, a person who already fulfilled his own obligation can still say them for others. The exceptions are ברכת הלחם and ברכת היין, which he can only say for others if he has not yet fulfilled them himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אהבה, the son of רבי זירא, taught: With all the blessings, even if a person already fulfilled his own obligation, he can still say them for others. The exceptions are the blessing over bread and the blessing over wine. For those, if he has not yet fulfilled his obligation, he can say them for others. But if he already fulfilled it, he cannot say them for others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about saying a ברכה for someone else. It gives a general rule and two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps asked who can be מוציא others with שופר. This ברייתא adds a new idea: having already fulfilled the מצוה yourself does not usually stop you from saying the ברכה for others. Bread and wine are different. There, only someone who has not yet made the ברכה for himself can make it for others.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught (a ברייתא)
He fulfilled his own obligation
He fulfills the obligation for others
The blessing over bread
The blessing over wine

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up יָצָא and מוֹצִיא. יָצָא means the person himself is already covered. מוֹצִיא means he covers someone else.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule. You can make most ברכות for others even after making them yourself, but not the ברכות on bread and wine.
steps.whatToRemember: General rule: someone who already said the ברכה can still say it for others. Exception: bread and wine, where only someone who has not yet said it can say it for others.

phrases.english: Ahava, son of Rabbi Zeira, taught:
All the blessings, every one of them,
even though he already fulfilled his obligation, he can fulfill it for others.
except for the blessing over bread and the blessing over wine,
where, if he has not fulfilled his obligation, he can fulfill it for others,
but if he already fulfilled it, he cannot fulfill it for others.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי אַהֲבָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of being מוציא others, moving from שופר to ברכות in general.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For most ברכות, one who already fulfilled his obligation can still be מוציא others. For ברכת הלחם and ברכת היין, he can be מוציא others only if he has not yet fulfilled his own obligation.

steps.title: רבא introduces a question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a question that רבא is about to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only opens a new question from רבא. The question itself comes next, so the גמרא is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בָּעֵי tells us that רבא has a real doubt and is not attacking anything. His question will most likely build on the rule we just learned about saying ברכות for others.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked, raised a doubt or question

phrases.english: Rava raised a question:

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a question that follows from the ברייתא of אהבה בריה דרבי זירא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The question itself is not stated yet. This line only introduces רבא's question.
